content.title: About
content.content: Canned Refried Beans are a ready‑to‑eat product made from cooked beans that are mashed into a paste and seasoned with spices. The vegetarian version contains no meat or animal fats and is typically packaged in airtight glass or metal cans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “refried” comes from the Spanish “refritos,” meaning “fried again.”
Traditionally refried beans are made from black or pinto beans, but canned versions often use a blend of beans.
Canned refried beans have a long shelf life—up to 2‑3 years when stored in a cool, dry place.
Vegetarian versions usually replace the traditional pork lard with vegetable oil or omit added fat altogether.
Refried beans are a staple in Mexican cuisine, used as a filling for burritos, tacos, chili, and as a side dish.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Beans provide about 7‑9 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Vegetarian canned versions typically contain less than 2 g of fat per 100 g, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for blood health and muscle function.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients in beans help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned products often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytates, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in large amounts.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Legumes can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Refried beans can be eaten straight from the can, warmed in the microwave or on the stove, used as a filling for tacos, burritos, chili, soups, or as a side dish with rice and vegetables. Feel free to add fresh herbs, lime juice, or hot sauce for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the beans in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
